Transition allowance: The existing one-second transition allowance is the maximum physical transition
duration from an issued command to its corresponding state: speed within ±2 rpm of the target after a
start command, or stationary paddle after a stop command. It is separate from the command-boundary
timing allowance. One allowance must not be reported as verification of the other.
Acceleration and deceleration mean that physical motion need not coincide exactly with the nominal
active interval. Brief post-command deceleration is a transition, not an additional scheduled stirring
interval.

This source specifies none of those study-level decisions and supplies
no sample-size justification.
Reused apparatus, runs conducted in the same session, or shared preparations may introduce
dependence. Within-run temperature samples must not be counted as independent replicates.
Causal conclusions cannot follow from procedural definitions alone. Even future observed differences
would require an appropriate comparison design and examination of alternative explanations. Findings
could not automatically generalize to other volumes, vessels, fluids, stirring geometries, ambient
conditions, or observation durations.
One synthetic specification without empirical observations is not evidence of a method effect or a
literature-wide research gap.

Check procedure: Use the task’s probe/logger configuration and the reference thermometer in
well-mixed water, with their sensing tips adjacent, no more than 5 mm apart, without contact with each
other or the container. Check two reference-temperature bands: 21–23 °C and 44–46 °C.
At each band, after readings have settled, record three paired probe/reference readings approximately
five seconds apart, spanning ten seconds. Each reference reading must fall within that band. Across the
three readings, the reference range and the probe range must each be no greater than 0.1 °C.
Proposed acceptance criterion: At both bands, every paired reading must satisfy:
|probe reading − reference reading| ≤ 0.2 °C.
Both bands must meet the temperature-band, stability, and agreement criteria.

The methods also differ in instantaneous speed and uninterrupted stirring
duration, so a future comparison could not isolate “intermittency alone.”
Probe lag, calibration error, timestamp error, vessel thermal history, residual exterior moisture, ambient
drift, and water loss could affect the recorded outcome. Equal nominal rotations do not remove these
limitations.
The two-temperature reference check evaluates limited agreement under its check conditions. It does not
establish absolute accuracy, response behavior during stirring, complete-range performance, or
measurement reliability across repeated runs. Reference uncertainty and temperature differences
between adjacent sensing tips remain relevant.

Section 8 — Untested research questions
1. Under the specified conditions, does the distribution of five-minute fixed-location temperature-drop
scores differ between continuous lower-speed stirring and intermittent higher-speed stirring?
2. How repeatable is the defined score across independently prepared fresh aliquots using each method?
These questions are unresolved within this document. They are not approved Research Gaps or selected
Hypotheses. No preferred direction, expected result, significance claim, or global novelty claim is
supplied.

It is not formal calibration, an uncertainty
budget, or proof of absolute measurement accuracy across the probe’s range.
Reference suitability: The reference thermometer must have reporting resolution of 0.1 °C or finer and
documented accuracy no worse than ±0.1 °C over 20–50 °C. Record its manufacturer/model, identifying
serial number or local instrument label, applicable accuracy specification, and current calibration or
verification status. A dated calibration or verification record must provide a documented basis for its
current suitability. Display resolution alone is insufficient.
Use only documentation that actually exists. This source supplies no certificate, calibration result, or
verified instrument performance.

Its purpose is to provide independently inspectable definitions of the task, methods,
measurement, assumptions, limitations, and unresolved questions.
This is not a real empirical study. No experimental results or fictional experimental observations
are reported. All numerical settings below are proposed procedural specifications, not observed values.
This case is independent of earlier synthetic documents. Its Method A, Method B, task, and score are
newly defined here; they do not recover the meanings of labels in an earlier corpus. No institution,
publication, author identity, DOI, or research citation is asserted.

Subtract without additional transformation,
normalization, absolute-value conversion, clipping, or averaging. Report S to one decimal place in
degrees Celsius of temperature difference.
Direction and interpretation: Positive S denotes a lower endpoint probe temperature; zero denotes no
change resolved by the recorded values; negative S denotes a higher endpoint probe temperature. A
larger score denotes a larger recorded temperature drop under these conditions. It does not
automatically designate a scientifically superior method.
Valid range: Both inputs must be finite and within 0–60 °C, and T0 must additionally meet the
starting-temperature requirement. Consequently, for a given valid T0, the numerical score lies between
T0 − 60 and T0.

Section 6 — Assumptions
Case-defining stipulations: The specified water volume, apparatus geometry, initial-temperature
window, environment, timing, stirring schedules, probe location, and score rule define this proposed
case. They are design choices, not experimental discoveries.
Assumptions requiring empirical confirmation:
- The chosen probe and logging arrangement can resolve temperature changes relevant to this
comparison.
- The preparation procedure produces sufficiently comparable initial thermal conditions, including vessel
temperature.
- The commanded stirring schedules can be reproduced within their stated tolerances.
- Differences between repeated preparations and environmental conditions can be documented
sufficiently for a meaningful comparison.

- An overhead stirrer with a vertical central shaft and one rectangular stainless-steel paddle, 20 ± 1 mm
wide and 10 ± 1 mm high. The paddle’s lower edge is fixed 5 ± 1 mm above the vessel’s internal base.
- A fixed temperature probe whose sensing tip is 15 ± 1 mm above the internal base and 20 ± 1 mm
horizontally from the shaft axis, without touching the vessel or paddle.
- A probe/logger with 0.1 °C reporting resolution, rated accuracy no worse than ±0.2 °C over 20–50 °C,
and rated 90% response time no longer than five seconds. Its certified measurement range must include
0–60 °C.
- A warming water bath, timer or synchronized controller, ambient thermometer, and a dry cork support
10 ± 1 mm thick.
- A reference thermometer meeting the pre-use requirements below.

Section 3 — Method A: Continuous low-speed paddle stirring
Method A is continuous clockwise paddle stirring at a commanded speed of 30 revolutions per minute
throughout the nominal interval from time zero to 300 seconds.
It requires the water, vessel, paddle, probe placement, preparation, reference-check eligibility, and
environment defined in Section 2. The paddle remains immersed and is not repositioned during the run.
Start the motor immediately after recording T0; stop it only after recording T300.
The speed setting, uninterrupted operation, direction, geometry, and five-minute duration define Method
A. The nominal schedule specifies 150 paddle revolutions by integrating the commanded speed over the
nominal interval. This is schedule arithmetic, not an observed revolution count.

Experimental and observation unit: One fresh water aliquot undergoing one uninterrupted five-minute
run with one stirring method. Temperature samples within a run are repeated measurements of that unit,
not independent experimental units.
Necessary materials and apparatus:
- An open, straight-sided cylindrical borosilicate glass vessel with internal diameter 70 ± 2 mm, wall
thickness 2 ± 0.5 mm, and capacity sufficient for 100 mL without overflow.
- 100 ± 1 mL of deionized water per run, measured with a graduated cylinder.
- An overhead stirrer with a vertical central shaft and one rectangular stainless-steel paddle, 20 ± 1 mm
wide and 10 ± 1 mm high. The paddle’s lower edge is fixed 5 ± 1 mm above the vessel’s internal base.

It does not
establish absolute accuracy, response behavior during stirring, complete-range performance, or
measurement reliability across repeated runs. Reference uncertainty and temperature differences
between adjacent sensing tips remain relevant.
Command logs and rated motor performance do not themselves measure actual speed, transition
duration, or revolution totals. Without suitable existing feedback, some physical adherence requirements
may remain unverified. No equality of mechanical work or energy input follows from nominal rotation
totals.
A future comparison would require human decisions about allocation, run order, replication, apparatus
reuse, and confounding control. This source specifies none of those study-level decisions and supplies
no sample-size justification.

Section 5 — Outcome and scoring
Measured construct: Five-minute temperature drop at the fixed probe location. This is an operational
temperature measure, not a direct measure of total heat lost, energy efficiency, or uniform bulk-water
temperature.
Observation unit: One conforming run with one fresh aliquot.
Observable scoring inputs: The logged initial temperature T0 and the logged temperature T300, both in
degrees Celsius, together with their timestamps, reference-check association, and procedural-validity
record.
Exact derivation rule:
Temperature-drop score S = T0 − T300.
Use the recorded temperatures at their 0.1 °C resolution. Subtract without additional transformation,
normalization, absolute-value conversion, clipping, or averaging.

The nominal schedule specifies 150 paddle revolutions by integrating the commanded speed over the
nominal interval. This is schedule arithmetic, not an observed revolution count.
Commands, transitions, and adherence records
Commanded versus actual speed: A 30-rpm setting is a command. A display that repeats the setting is
not necessarily a measurement of actual paddle speed. Record whether any available speed feedback is
measured, controller-estimated, or merely the commanded setting.
Schedule boundaries: The start command must follow T0 and occur within one second of time zero.
The stop command has a nominal boundary of 300 seconds, must occur within one second of that
boundary, and must follow capture of T300.

Valid range: Both inputs must be finite and within 0–60 °C, and T0 must additionally meet the
starting-temperature requirement. Consequently, for a given valid T0, the numerical score lies between
T0 − 60 and T0. These are input-validity bounds, not predictions about physical behavior. Do not clamp
unexpected values into this range.
Measurement occasion: T0 is captured immediately before stirring begins. T300 is the scheduled
300-second sample, captured before Method A’s final stop command; Method B is already stationary.
Endpoint timestamps must be within one second of their scheduled occasions. Motor command
allowances do not shift the endpoint measurement occasion.
Repeated observations: Intermediate one-second samples preserve the temperature trace but do not
contribute to S.

Section 4 — Method B: Intermittent higher-speed paddle stirring
Method B is clockwise paddle stirring at a commanded speed of 60 revolutions per minute during these
five nominal active intervals, expressed in seconds after time zero:
[0, 30), [60, 90), [120, 150), [180, 210), and [240, 270).
The paddle is commanded to stop during all intervening intervals, including [270, 300]. It remains
immersed and in the same position throughout.
Method B independently requires the water, vessel, paddle, probe placement, preparation,
reference-check eligibility, and environment defined in Section 2. Initiate the first active interval
immediately after recording T0. Capture T300 while the paddle is stationary; issue no new stirring
command at 300 seconds.

Repeated observations: Intermediate one-second samples preserve the temperature trace but do not
contribute to S. There is one score per run. Repeated runs retain separate scores; this document defines
no across-run aggregation.
Missing or invalid observations: If either endpoint is absent, non-finite, outside the stated range, or
outside its timing allowance, no valid score is available. Do not interpolate, substitute another timestamp,
or impute a value.
Keep endpoint validity, reference-check eligibility, and method-adherence status distinct. A failed or
incomplete reference check makes the run instrument-ineligible. A documented procedural violation
makes it nonconforming. Insufficient verification of an identity-defining motor requirement makes method
conformity unverified.

It does not retroactively validate
runs associated with a failed or incomplete check. A change affecting temperature measurement after a
pass requires another complete check.
Preparation and run requirements
Preparation and required actions: Fill the vessel with a fresh aliquot. With the stationary paddle and
probe immersed in their specified positions, condition the vessel in the warming bath until the probe
reads 45.0 ± 0.2 °C and changes by no more than 0.1 °C over ten seconds. Remove the vessel, dry its
exterior, and place it on the cork support.
Within ten seconds of removal, record the initial probe temperature as T0 while the paddle is stationary.
T0 must be within 44.8–45.2 °C. That recording defines time zero; immediately initiate the chosen stirring
schedule.
